answers.d01: 似然回答：假设成立时，看到手头这批数据的概率多大。后验回答：看到数据之后，假设成立的概率多大。方向相反：似然由因推果，后验由果推因。例：一枚硬币，候选假设「正面概率0.5」与「正面概率0.3」，先验各占一半。抛10次出3次正面：L(0.5)=C(10,3)×0.5¹⁰≈0.117，L(0.3)=C(10,3)×0.3³×0.7⁷≈0.267。这两个数只是各自假设产生这批数据的可能性。要得后验，用贝叶斯：P(0.5|数据)=0.117/(0.117+0.267)≈30%——先验各半被这批数据改写成了30%对70%。两点提醒：似然数值本身不说明假设成立，比较几个假设才有意义；数据有限时，较高的似然也不等于证实。后验还额外依赖先验，这正是两者的分工。
answers.d02: The average gives the center of the data; variance measures how far values spread around that center. For a whole population: σ² = (1/N) Σ (xᵢ − μ)². Take each value, subtract the mean μ (its deviation), square it, then average the squares. Example: {4, 5, 6} has mean 5, deviations −1, 0, 1, variance (1+0+1)/3 ≈ 0.67. {0, 5, 10} has the same mean but variance (25+0+25)/3 ≈ 16.7 — same center, far more spread. Squaring serves two jobs: it stops +1 and −1 from cancelling to zero, and it punishes large deviations harder. The price: units get squared (kg²), so we usually take the square root — the standard deviation — to return to kg. Why squares rather than absolute values? Both remove signs; squaring is the conventional choice, smooth and mathematically convenient, not a logical necessity. It also makes variance sensitive to outliers: replace 6 with 100 and it explodes.
answers.d03: 正反馈指输出的结果反过来加强输入，使变化沿原方向越滚越大。话筒对准音箱是例子：一点杂音被放大，从音箱播出，又进话筒，再放大，几秒内变成刺耳啸叫。这里的「正」指方向相同——偏差被放大——而不是「好」。被放大的是什么决定好坏：金融市场上，涨吸引买入，涨得更凶，泡沫就这样吹大；跌引发恐慌抛售，跌得更深。同一机制也可能有用，关键看能否装上刹车：把话筒拿开、给市场设涨跌停，都是在回路里削弱这个自我加强。放大不会无限继续——音箱功率有上限、资金有限——撞到天花板后就稳定、振荡或崩溃。和负反馈对照最清楚：空调温度高了就制冷，偏差被压回；正反馈把偏差推得更远。判断关键：看系统是回到原点还是加速偏离，再把「机制方向」与「结果好坏」分开评价。
answers.d04: Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you give up when you choose one. Suppose your free afternoon has three uses: a nap (worth a night of good rest), tutoring for $40, or finishing a course you value like $30. If you choose tutoring, the opportunity cost is not $70 — it is only the value of the single best forgone option, the nap. Common mistake: adding up everything rejected; you could only have done one anyway. And a 'free' afternoon is never free: scrolling social media for three hours costs the $40 you could have earned. Condition change: if you're exhausted, the nap becomes the best alternative, so working now costs more than the $40 — resting is the rational pick. The habit it builds: judge every choice against what you would actually do instead, not against doing nothing.
answers.d05: 某病患病率是千分之一，检测很准：患者99%呈阳性，健康人也有5%被误报。某人查出阳性，他真患病的概率是多少？直觉答99%，实际约2%。算一下：让10万人去检测。患者100人，约99人阳性；健康99900人，误报约4995人阳性。阳性共约5094人，真正的患者只占99/5094≈2%。这么低的原因：健康人基数巨大，5%的误报乘上它，把患者的阳性淹没了。贝叶斯公式 P(病|阳)=P(阳|病)×P(病)/P(阳) 说的正是这一步：把「检测的准确率」换成「拿到阳性证据后的患病概率」。条件变化：换到患病率10%的高危人群，同一检测下阳性者约69%真患病。同样的证据，先验不同，结论差得远——这就是先验在起作用。
answers.d06: A cache keeps a nearby copy of slow-to-fetch data — say the rendered profile page — so repeat visits are fast. The catch: the user edits their bio, but the cache still holds the old page, and visitors see stale data. Cache invalidation is removing or refreshing such stale copies so the cache matches the source of truth. Two common strategies. TTL: every entry expires after, say, 60 seconds — simple, but data can be stale for up to a minute, and the database absorbs the refresh load. Active invalidation: when the user saves a new bio, the app explicitly deletes the cached profile — fresh immediately, but you must catch every write path, including admin edits and batch jobs; miss one and users see stale data indefinitely. That is why it's called one of the hard problems of computing: the copy must track a source it doesn't control.
answers.d07: 冰激凌销量高的月份，溺水人数也多，两者强相关，但吃冰激凌不会让人溺水。共同原因是气温：天热既让人多买冷饮，也让人多下水。这类隐藏的共同原因叫混杂因素。区分的依据：因果要求「改变A，B通过A这条通路跟着变」。做法是把共同原因固定住——只在天同样热的日子比较冰激凌销量和溺水数，若相关消失，原相关就是混杂造成的；若仍在，才更接近因果。更硬的办法是随机分组：随机让人吃或不吃冰激凌，看溺水是否还跟着变。另外还要问一句方向：会不会是溺水多导致冰激凌卖多？日常迁移：吃某保健品的人恢复更快，可能只是买得起的人本身体质就好——不固定「体质」这个共同原因，相关照样冒充因果。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth feeds on itself: each gain is added to the base, and the next gain is computed on the bigger base. A = P(1+r)^t. $100 at 10% a year: year 1 earns $10 → $110; year 2 earns $11, not $10 → $121. That extra $1 is interest on interest. After 30 years, $100 becomes about $1,745, versus $400 with simple interest. Why the starting amount matters: the rate is relative, so the same 10% multiplies whatever base exists. $10,000 earns $1,000 the first year while $100 earns $10 — and the gap itself then compounds, widening every year. This is why starting ten years earlier at 7% roughly doubles the final amount: time sits in the exponent, amplifying both the rate and the principal. It cuts both ways: credit-card debt compounds against you by the same arithmetic.
answers.v01: 过拟合：模型把训练数据的细节和噪声背了下来，而不是学到真正管用的规律，结果在新数据上反而差。用一个对应关系类比：学生死记每道练习题的答案，练习册全对；考试换个数字就不会——他记住的是「这题选B」，不是「这类题怎么解」。机器学习里同样：预测房价的模型若足够「自由」，能记住训练集里纯属巧合的细节，训练误差降到0，换一批房就错得离谱。判断依据正是这个落差：训练表现好、新数据表现差。条件变化：数据越多，巧合细节越难背全，过拟合越轻；模型越复杂、数据越少，过拟合越重。所以常用做法是留出一部分数据专供「考试」、限制模型复杂度。代价：管得太死会连规律也学不会，即欠拟合，好模型取中间。
answers.v02: Search a library of 100 documents for 'diabetes'; exactly 10 are relevant. Your system returns 15 documents, 8 of them relevant. Precision = 8/15 ≈ 53%: of what I returned, how much was right. Recall = 8/10 = 80%: of everything that exists, how much I found. They answer different questions — precision is the trustworthiness of each result, recall is what was missed. Changing the retrieval threshold flips the balance: return 60 documents to catch all 10 relevant ones and recall hits 100%, but precision falls to ~17%. Which matters more depends on cost: a spam filter prizes precision (a lost real email is costly); cancer screening prizes recall (a missed case is costly). The same arithmetic applies to any retrieval or classification task: correctness among your selections versus coverage of the true set.
answers.v03: 自然选择里没有谁在「努力变强」，只有谁能留下更多后代的差别。说长颈鹿拼命伸脖子所以脖子变长，是错的。过程分三步：先有随机变异——同代鹿天生脖子有长有短，变异不针对任何目标；然后环境做筛选——低处叶子吃光时，长颈鹿吃得更多、活得更久，留下更多继承长颈的后代；于是下一代里「长颈」基因的比例升高。变的是种群的基因构成，不是某只鹿在一生中变长。条件变化：如果矮处食物充足，长颈的优势消失，比例不再上升，甚至因生育成本下降；环境一变，筛选标准跟着变。迁移到细菌：种群中天然存在极少数耐药个体，抗生素并不「制造」耐药性，只是把不耐药的大量杀死，耐药者占据下一代——这正是滥用抗生素催生耐药菌的机制。
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent when performing it many times has the same effect as performing it once. Distributed systems make this matter because retries are unavoidable: a client calls POST /charge, the network drops the response, the client retries — without idempotency the customer is billed twice. Classify by effect: SET x=5 is idempotent (repeating changes nothing); x = x+1 and list.append(item) are not (each retry adds one more). The standard fix: the client attaches a unique idempotency key to the request; the server records processed keys and, on a repeat, returns the stored result instead of redoing the work. Condition change: idempotency depends on scope — SET x=5 is idempotent, SET x=now() is not, since each call yields a different value. Rule of thumb: assume every write will eventually be duplicated, and design it to tolerate that.
answers.v05: 信息熵衡量结果揭晓前你有多难猜：H = −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ，pᵢ 是每种结果的概率，−log pᵢ 是该结果出现时的意外程度，熵就是平均意外，以2为底时单位是比特。均匀概率最不确定：硬币两面各半，熵为1比特；若两面都是正面（p=1），熵为0，你必然猜中，毫无悬念。原因在于：概率集中在某个结果上时，你猜它常常猜中，平均意外低；概率越摊平，任何猜法都容易错。数值对比：四选一均匀，熵为2比特；若概率是(1/2, 1/4, 1/4)，熵只有1.5比特——一半时候你猜第一个就对。条件变化：结果数固定时均匀给最大熵；结果数增多，均匀熵随之增大，八面均匀骰是3比特。熵描述的是猜之前的不确定性，不是事情本身乱不乱。
answers.v06: Deadlock: a group of processes each hold resources and each wait for a resource another one holds, so none can ever proceed. Example: Process A holds the database lock and now requests the file lock; Process B holds the file lock and requests the database lock. A waits for B, B waits for A — both stuck forever, though neither is 'wrong'. Deadlock needs four conditions at once: mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait. That gives the fixes: break any one. If B releases the file lock before asking for the database (no hold-and-wait), the trap disappears. Common engineering rules follow: a global lock order — everyone locks database first, file second, making a cycle impossible — or timeouts that abort one process. Contrast an ordinary wait: if the resource will simply be freed, patience pays; in a circle of waits, it never can.
answers.v07: 公共物品是人人可享用、一个人用也不减少别人份额的东西，路灯是典型：无法只照亮付钱的人，多一个人走路不费灯。麻烦正出在这里——不付钱也被照亮，于是人人想搭便车：等别人出钱，自己白享。设想一栋楼十户，装路灯共花500元，每户受益值100元。装了大家都赚，可每户都会想：我不出钱，灯大概率照样装。十户都这么想，灯就装不成，每户白白损失100元。每个人理性的选择，加总成对所有人糟糕的结果，这就是公共物品难靠自愿供给的原因。人数少、互相盯得见时好办，业委会能收钱；人多、匿名时（如温室气体减排）就难，所以通常靠税收强制出资。注意对照：电梯虽共用却能收费，不算严格公共物品。
answers.v08: Little's Law says L = λW: in a stable system, the average number of items inside (L) equals the arrival rate (λ) times the average time each item spends inside (W). Coffee shop: customers arrive at 10 per minute and each stays 4 minutes, so on average 40 people are in the shop. The practical power lies in what you needn't measure: count arrivals and duration (easy) to infer occupancy (hard), or run it backward — if the shop holds 40 and each visit lasts 4 minutes, throughput must be 10 per minute. It requires stability: arrivals equal departures, so the queue isn't growing without bound. Condition change: speed up service so each stay is 2 minutes while arrivals stay 10 per minute, and occupancy falls to 20 — halving service time halves the crowd. The same equation counts requests on a server or tickets in a backlog.
